The right node connects four branches: the 5 A current coming from the left enters the right node; the upper branch is labeled I2, with the arrow pointing downward, indicating entering the right node; the 10 A arrow of the right branch points right, indicating leaving the right node; the 2 A arrow of the lower branch points downward, indicating leaving the right node. Reasoning: Apply KCL to the left node according to the specified method. I1 entering the left node equals the sum of the three currents leaving the left node, so I1 = 3 A + 10 A + 5 A = 18 A. Apply KCL to the right node. The currents entering the right node are 5 A and I2, and the currents leaving the right node are 10 A and 2 A, so 5 A + I2 = 10 A + 2 A = 12 A, obtaining I2 = 7 A. Comparison gives 18 A > 7 A, therefore I1 is greater than I2.
